biography: Luis Carlos Zapelini, a name whispered with respect in the Opala Old Stock Race paddocks, hails from the sun-drenched orange groves of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. His journey began not on asphalt, but on the dusty dirt tracks carving through his family's farm, where he honed his car control skills in a beat-up Willys Jeep. Racing wasn't a family tradition; it was a personal obsession ignited by grainy broadcasts of Senna's exploits. Zapelini's break came unexpectedly when he impressed a local Opala team owner with his raw talent during an impromptu 'qualifying session' on a public road. He quickly proved his mettle, scoring a surprise podium in his debut season. However, recent years have seen a dip in form. Once a consistent frontrunner, Zapelini now struggles to maintain his position, fueling speculation about his future in the sport.
drivingStyle: Zapelini is a calculating driver, known for his precise lines and meticulous tire management. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes; instead, he prefers to patiently stalk his prey, waiting for the opportune moment to strike with surgical precision. He's a master of defensive driving, making it notoriously difficult for rivals to pass him. While he excels in longer races where tire conservation is crucial, he sometimes lacks the outright aggression needed for short, sprint-style events.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision in the 2018 Interlagos round, where Oliveira accused Zapelini of deliberately wrecking him.

Their rivalry is built on mutual respect, but also fierce competition for the title of 'Best Opala Driver' in Brazil. They've traded wins and podiums for years, creating a captivating on-track spectacle.
Silva, a veteran of the series, often criticizes Zapelini's 'overly cautious' driving style, leading to heated exchanges in post-race interviews.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother before every race.
Refuses to eat anything orange on race day, believing it brings bad luck.
Spends exactly 15 minutes meticulously cleaning his helmet visor before each session.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about raw speed; it's about making the right decisions at the right time. It's a chess game on wheels."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2017 Opala Old Stock Race Championship after a season-long battle with his arch-rival, Ricardo Oliveira. He clinched the title with a nail-biting victory in the final race at Curitiba.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2020 Interlagos 500, costing him a potential victory and severely damaging his championship hopes. The incident was attributed to a rare lapse in concentration.
